Are deemed to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (Section 56), and are not compellable, in proceedings to which they are not a party, to produce the register or to give evidence about matters coming to their knowledge in official capacity except by order of the court for special cause (Section 70)
questions.explanation: These provisions protect the integrity of the registration process.

questions.question_text: Under Section 23 of the GI Act, 1999, the certificate of registration of a geographical indication granted by the Registrar:
options: Has no evidentiary value in court
Must always be proved through the original document
Is prima facie evidence of the validity of the registration and is admissible in all courts before whom it is produced without further proof or production of the original
Is conclusive proof binding on all courts and cannot be challenged
questions.explanation: Section 23 makes the registration certificate only prima facie (not conclusive) evidence of validity, so it can still be challenged in rectification or infringement proceedings; Section 23(2) clarifies that this does not affect the right of action for an unregistered GI (passing off).

questions.question_text: Under the GI Act, 1999, the benefit of a registered geographical indication accrues to:
options: All the producers in the defined geographical region who make the goods according to the registered standards and who become registered authorised users — GI protection is therefore a tool of rural and community development
questions.explanation: This collective, region-linked benefit is what distinguishes a GI from a trade mark, which identifies a single commercial source.

questions.question_text: Under Section 2(1)(k) of the GI Act, 1999, 'producer' in relation to goods includes:
options: Any person who, if the goods are agricultural, produces or processes or packages them; if natural goods, exploits them; and if handicraft or industrial goods, makes or manufactures them — and includes any person who trades or deals in such production, exploitation, making or manufacturing
questions.explanation: The wide definition ensures that all links in the regional value chain can be authorised users.

questions.question_text: Under Section 82 of the GI Act, 1999, a declaration as to title to a geographical indication:
options: Must be registered under the Registration Act, 1908
Is registrable only with the Registrar of Companies
Is not registrable as a document under the Registration Act, 1908 (because a GI is a collective right and not the private property of any one person)
questions.explanation: This reinforces the non-proprietary, community character of a geographical indication.

questions.question_text: Under Section 16 of the GI Act, 1999, the registration of a geographical indication takes effect from:
options: The date the certificate is issued
The date the first authorised user is registered
The date of filing of the application, and that date is deemed to be the date of registration
questions.explanation: Back-dating the registration to the application date fixes the priority position of the GI.

questions.question_text: Under Section 11(6) read with Section 13 of the GI Act, 1999, after examination the Registrar:
options: May accept the application absolutely, or subject to conditions or limitations, or may refuse it — and the accepted application is advertised in the Geographical Indications Journal for opposition
Must accept every application as filed
Refers the application to the Central Government
questions.explanation: Opposition may be filed within the prescribed period (three months, extendable) after advertisement (Section 14); acceptance may separately be withdrawn before registration under Section 12 if it was made in error.

questions.question_text: India's protection of geographical indications helps prevent 'bio-piracy' and misappropriation, illustrated by the earlier controversies over foreign attempts to obtain exclusive rights over:
options: Basmati rice (a US patent later substantially curtailed) and turmeric and neem (US/EPO patents revoked for lack of novelty over Indian traditional knowledge)
questions.explanation: These episodes spurred India to build the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library and to strengthen GI protection; 'Basmati' is now a registered Indian GI.

questions.question_text: Under Section 18(5) of the GI Act, 1999, where a geographical indication has been removed from the register for non-payment of the renewal fee:
options: It automatically revives after one year

The Registrar may, after six months and within one year from the expiration of the last registration, on receipt of an application in the prescribed form and payment of the prescribed fee, restore it and renew its registration if satisfied that it is just to do so
Only the Central Government can restore it
questions.explanation: Separately, Section 19 treats a removed GI, for the purpose of later applications by others, as one already on the register for one year after removal, to prevent immediate misappropriation.

questions.question_text: Under Section 7(1) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, the Court may make an order appointing or declaring a guardian of a minor if it is satisfied that it is for the:
questions.explanation: Section 7(1) explicitly specifies that the sole basis for appointing/declaring a guardian is the welfare of the minor.

questions.question_text: Under Section 9(1) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, which District Court has jurisdiction to entertain an application for guardianship of the PERSON of a minor?
options: The District Court where the father resides
The District Court where property is located
The District Court having jurisdiction in the place where the minor ORDINARILY RESIDES
The High Court of the State capital
questions.explanation: Section 9(1) strictly anchors person guardianship jurisdiction to where the minor ordinarily resides.

questions.question_text: Under Section 9(2) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, an application for guardianship of the PROPERTY of a minor may be made to:
options: Only where the property is situated
Either the District Court where the minor ordinarily resides OR the District Court where the property is situated
questions.explanation: Section 9(2) gives dual jurisdiction options for property guardianship: ordinary residence or property location.

questions.question_text: Under Section 17(1) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, in appointing or declaring a guardian of a minor, the Court shall be guided by what paramount consideration?
options: What, consistently with the law to which the minor is subject, appears in the circumstances to be for the WELFARE OF THE MINOR
The financial status of the father
The religious vow of the guardian
The preference of the maternal uncle
questions.explanation: Section 17(1) enacts that child welfare consistent with personal law is the guiding principle.

questions.question_text: Under Section 17(3) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, if the minor is old enough to form an intelligent preference, may the Court consider the minor's preference?
options: No, minor's preference is completely ignored
Yes, the Court MAY consider the preference of the minor
questions.explanation: Section 17(3) empowers the court to consider the preference of an intelligent minor.

questions.question_text: Under Section 19(b) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (as substituted in 2010), the Court is NOT authorized to appoint or declare a guardian of the person of a minor (other than a married female) whose father or mother is living UNLESS:
options: That parent works in another state
That parent is, in the opinion of the Court, unfit to be guardian of the person of the minor
questions.explanation: Section 19(b), as substituted by Act 30 of 2010, bars the court from appointing a guardian where a living father or mother is not, in the opinion of the court, unfit.

questions.question_text: Under Section 25(1) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, if a ward leaves or is removed from the custody of a guardian of his person, the Court may make an order for the ward's return to custody IF satisfied that:
options: The ward is under 5 years old
It will be for the welfare of the ward to return to the custody of his guardian
questions.explanation: Section 25(1) conditions custody return orders on the welfare of the ward.

questions.question_text: Under Section 29 of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, a court-appointed or declared guardian of property CANNOT, without previous permission of the Court, lease any part of the minor's immovable property for a term exceeding:
options: Five years, or for any term extending more than one year beyond the date on which the ward will attain majority
questions.explanation: Section 29 limits lease terms to 5 years (or 1 year post-majority) without court permission.

questions.question_text: Under Section 29(a) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, a court-appointed guardian of property CANNOT sell, mortgage, charge, or exchange any part of the minor's immovable property without:
questions.explanation: Section 29(a) mandates prior court permission for selling/mortgaging minor's immovable property.

questions.question_text: Under Section 30 of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, any disposal of immovable property by a guardian in contravention of Section 28 or Section 29 is:
options: Voidable at the instance of any other person affected thereby (including the minor)
questions.explanation: Section 30 explicitly renders unauthorized property transfers voidable (not void ab initio).

questions.question_text: Under Section 31(1) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, the Court shall NOT grant permission to a guardian under Section 29 EXCEPT in case of:
options: Necessity or for an evident advantage to the minor
questions.explanation: Section 31(1) strictly limits court permission to necessity or evident advantage of minor.

questions.question_text: Under Section 20(1) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, what is the legal nature of the relationship between a guardian and his ward?
options: A fiduciary relation, and the guardian must not make any profit out of his office
questions.explanation: Section 20(1) defines guardian-ward relationship as fiduciary prohibiting personal profit.

questions.question_text: Under Section 26(1) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, a guardian of the person appointed or declared by the Court shall NOT remove the ward from the limits of the Court's jurisdiction WITHOUT:
options: Leave of the Court (except for temporary purposes)
questions.explanation: Section 26(1) forbids permanent removal of ward from jurisdiction without leave of court.

questions.question_text: Under Section 39 of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, the Court may REMOVE a guardian appointed or declared by it on which of the following grounds?
options: Abuse of trust, continuous failure to perform duties, ill-treatment of ward, conviction of offence showing defect of character, or adverse interest
questions.explanation: Section 39 lists statutory grounds for removing a guardian including breach of trust and misconduct.

questions.question_text: Under Section 41(1)(d) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, the powers of a guardian of the PERSON cease upon the marriage of a female ward TO:
options: A husband who is not, in the opinion of the Court, unfit to be guardian of her person
questions.explanation: Section 41(1)(d) provides person guardianship ceases upon marriage of female ward to non-unfit husband.

questions.question_text: In Rosy Jacob v. Jacob A. Chakramakkal (1973) 1 SCC 840, the Supreme Court held regarding custody under Section 25 of the Guardians and Wards Act that:
options: The controlling consideration in custody disputes is the welfare of the children, and technical legal rights of parents must yield to child welfare
Father's legal right is absolute regardless of welfare
Custody is decided by drawing lots
questions.explanation: Rosy Jacob (1973) established child welfare as the dominant consideration overriding parental rights.
questions.statute_or_case: Rosy Jacob v. Jacob A. Chakramakkal (1973) 1 SCC 840

questions.question_text: In Nil Ratan Kundu v. Abhijit Kundu (2008) 9 SCC 413, the Supreme Court emphasized that in determining custody under GWA 1890, the court acts in:
options: Parens Patriae jurisdiction, where the child's welfare is the sole paramount factor
questions.explanation: Nil Ratan Kundu (2008) held custody proceedings exercise parens patriae jurisdiction for child welfare.
questions.statute_or_case: Nil Ratan Kundu v. Abhijit Kundu (2008) 9 SCC 413

questions.question_text: Under Section 47 of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, an APPEAL lies to the High Court against an order of the District Court:
options: Appointing, declaring, or refusing to appoint or declare a guardian under Section 7, or removing a guardian under Section 39
questions.explanation: Section 47 lists appealable orders to the High Court.

questions.question_text: Under Section 44 of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, if a person unlawfully removes a ward from the jurisdiction of the Court in violation of Section 26, he is punishable with:
options: Fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or imprisonment for a term up to six months
questions.explanation: Section 44 penalizes unlawful removal of ward with fine up to Rs. 1,000 or 6 months jail.

questions.question_text: Under Section 45(1) of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, if a guardian fails to produce the minor or file accounts/inventory when ordered, the Court may impose:
options: A fine not exceeding one hundred rupees, plus a further fine up to ten rupees for each day of continued default (maximum five hundred rupees in the aggregate), and detention in the civil jail until compliance
A fine of ten rupees only
A fixed fine of five thousand rupees
A fine of fifty thousand rupees
questions.explanation: Section 45(1) allows a fine up to Rs. 100, a further Rs. 10 per day (subject to a Rs. 500 aggregate cap), and civil detention until the default is remedied.

questions.question_text: Under Section 4(1) of GWA 1890, a 'minor' means a person who has NOT attained majority under the provisions of:
questions.explanation: Section 4(1) references Indian Majority Act 1875 for minor definition.

questions.question_text: Under Section 3 of the Indian Majority Act, 1875 (as amended), a minor for whom a guardian has been appointed by a Court under GWA 1890 attains majority at the age of:
questions.explanation: Following 1999 amendment to Majority Act, majority age is 18 years across board.

questions.question_text: Under Section 12(1) of GWA 1890, the Court may make such interlocutory order as it thinks fit for the temporary custody and protection of the person or property of the minor:
options: At any time after the admission of an application for guardianship
questions.explanation: Section 12(1) authorizes interim/interlocutory protection orders anytime post-admission.

questions.question_text: Under Section 14 of GWA 1890, if applications for guardianship of the same minor are filed in two DIFFERENT District Courts, which Court proceeds?
options: The Court in which application was FIRST admitted proceeds, and the other Court stays proceedings pending first Court's decision
questions.explanation: Section 14 prevents conflicting orders by giving priority to court where application was first admitted.

questions.question_text: Under Section 15(1) of GWA 1890, can the Court appoint MORE THAN ONE guardian of a minor's person or property?
options: Yes, the Court may appoint or declare several guardians of the person or property or both
Only if guardians are husband and wife
questions.explanation: Section 15(1) allows appointing joint/multiple guardians.

questions.question_text: Under Section 21 of GWA 1890, a minor is incompetent to act as guardian of any minor EXCEPT:
options: His own wife or child (or where he is managing member of undivided Hindu family)
questions.explanation: Section 21 creates narrow exception allowing minor to be guardian of spouse/child.

questions.question_text: Under Section 27 of GWA 1890, what is the standard of care required of a guardian of a minor's property?
options: He is bound to deal with property as carefully as a man of ordinary prudence would deal with it if it were his own
questions.explanation: Section 27 imposes the 'ordinary prudent owner' standard of care.

questions.question_text: Under Section 34(b) of GWA 1890, a court-appointed property guardian must, if required by the Court, deliver a statement (inventory) of the minor's property within what time after appointment?
options: Within six months from date of appointment (or such other time as court directs)
questions.explanation: Section 34(b) requires delivery of the statement of the ward's property within six months of appointment (or such other time as the Court directs).

questions.question_text: Under Section 38 of GWA 1890, on the death of one of joint guardians:
options: The guardianship continues to the survivor or survivors until another guardian is appointed
questions.explanation: Section 38 enacts right of survivorship among joint guardians.

questions.question_text: Under Section 40(1) of GWA 1890, a guardian appointed or declared by the Court may apply to be DISCHARGED from his office IF:
options: He desires to resign and court finds sufficient reason
questions.explanation: Section 40(1) allows guardian to seek voluntary discharge for sufficient reasons.

questions.question_text: Under Section 4A(1) of GWA 1890, the High Court or District Judge may transfer guardianship proceedings to:
options: Any subordinate judicial officer exercising original civil jurisdiction empowered in that behalf
questions.explanation: Section 4A authorizes transferring GWA proceedings to empowered subordinate civil judges.

questions.question_text: Under Section 8 of GWA 1890, who among the following is NOT entitled to apply for an order appointing a guardian?
options: A complete stranger having no interest or concern for minor
questions.explanation: Section 8 enumerates persons entitled to apply: prospective guardian, relative/friend, Collector.

questions.question_text: Under Section 10(1) of GWA 1890, an application for guardianship must be made by petition signed and verified in the manner prescribed by:
options: Code of Civil Procedure for verification of plaints
questions.explanation: Section 10(1) requires CPC plaints manner verification.

questions.question_text: Under Section 11(1) of GWA 1890, upon admission of guardianship application, notice of hearing must be served on:
options: Parents of minor, proposed guardian, and any person to whom special notice is directed by Court
questions.explanation: Section 11(1) mandates notice to parents, proposed guardian, and interested persons.

questions.question_text: Under Section 17(2) of GWA 1890, in considering what is for the welfare of the minor, the Court shall have regard to:
options: Financial net worth of guardian only
Age, sex, religion of minor, character & capacity of guardian, nearness of kin, and wishes of deceased parent
questions.explanation: Section 17(2) lists statutory welfare evaluation factors.

questions.question_text: Under Section 17(5) of GWA 1890, the Court shall NOT appoint or declare any person to be guardian against his:
questions.explanation: Section 17(5) prohibits the Court from appointing or declaring any person to be a guardian against his will (former sub-section (4) was omitted in 1951).

questions.question_text: Under Section 18 of GWA 1890, where the Court appoints a COLLECTOR as guardian of property, the Collector acts in virtue of his:
options: Office, and management is subject to rules of State Government
questions.explanation: Section 18 provides Collector acts ex-officio subject to government rules.

questions.question_text: Under Section 22(1) of GWA 1890, is a court-appointed guardian entitled to remuneration?
options: No, GWA service is strictly unpaid
Yes, guardian may receive such allowance for his care and trouble as the Court thinks fit
questions.explanation: Section 22(1) allows court to grant reasonable remuneration/allowance.

questions.question_text: Under Section 24 of GWA 1890, what is the core duty of a guardian of the person?
options: Charged with the custody of the ward and must look to his support, health, and education
questions.explanation: Section 24 defines person guardian's duty: custody, support, health, education.

questions.question_text: Under Section 28 of GWA 1890, what controls the powers of a TESTAMENTARY guardian (appointed by Will) to alienate minor's property?
options: The restrictions specified in the Will (unless court extends them under Section 32)
Court approval mandatory in all cases
questions.explanation: Section 28 provides testamentary guardian's powers are governed by Will terms.

questions.question_text: Under Section 31(2) of GWA 1890, when Court grants permission to sell minor's property under Section 29, what order details does it specify?
options: Necessity/advantage, floor price, public auction or private sale, and application of sale proceeds
questions.explanation: Section 31(2) details protective conditions required in court permission orders.

questions.question_text: Under Section 33(1) of GWA 1890, a court-appointed guardian of property may apply by petition to the Court for:
options: Opinion, advice, or direction on any present question respecting management or administration of ward's property
questions.explanation: Section 33(1) allows guardian to seek court's advisory direction on property management.

questions.question_text: Under Section 34(c) of GWA 1890, a property guardian must exhibit accounts of his receipts and disbursements in Court at such times as:
questions.explanation: Section 34(c) requires the guardian to exhibit his accounts in Court at such times and in such form as the Court from time to time directs.

questions.question_text: Under Section 35 of GWA 1890, if a guardian breaches an administration bond executed under Section 34(a), who may sue on the bond?
options: Any person assigned the bond by Court, or a successor guardian, or the minor on attaining majority
questions.explanation: Section 35 authorizes court to assign administration bond for enforcing liability.

questions.question_text: Under Section 37 of GWA 1890, does anything in Section 35 or 36 exempt a guardian from general liability as a trustee for breach of trust?
options: Yes, execution of bond exempts him
No, Section 37 preserves general trustee liability of guardian for breach of trust
questions.explanation: Section 37 explicitly saves general fiduciary liability as a trustee.

questions.question_text: Under Section 41(2) of GWA 1890, the authority of a guardian of PROPERTY ceases by his death, removal, discharge, or by:
questions.explanation: Section 41(2) provides property guardianship terminates upon ward reaching majority.

questions.question_text: Under Section 43 of GWA 1890, the Court may make an order regulating the conduct or proceedings of a guardian. If the guardian disobeys such an order, how is it enforced?
options: By automatic removal of the minor to State care
In the same manner as an injunction granted under the Code of Civil Procedure, as if the ward were the plaintiff and the guardian the defendant
questions.explanation: Section 43(4) provides that disobedience of an order under Section 43 may be enforced in the same manner as disobedience of an injunction under the CPC.

questions.question_text: Under Section 48 of GWA 1890, an order made under the Act shall be FINAL and shall NOT be liable to be contested by:
questions.explanation: Section 48 bars collateral civil suits challenging GWA orders.

questions.question_text: Under Section 50 of GWA 1890, who has rule-making power to prescribe procedures, forms, and fees under the Act?
questions.explanation: Section 50 empowers the High Court to make rules.

questions.question_text: In Yashita Sahu v. State of Rajasthan (2020) 3 SCC 67, the Supreme Court held regarding child custody and contact rights of non-custodial parent:
options: Non-custodial parent must never see child
Child is entitled to the love and affection of both parents; non-custodial parent must be granted sufficient visitation and contact rights (physical/virtual)
questions.explanation: Yashita Sahu (2020) affirmed child's right to access both parents and contact rights of non-custodial parent.
questions.statute_or_case: Yashita Sahu v. State of Rajasthan (2020) 3 SCC 67

questions.question_text: Under Section 1(1) of Act No. 8 of 1890, the short title is:
questions.explanation: Section 1(1) defines exact short title.

questions.question_text: Under Section 1(3) of GWA 1890, the Act came into force on:
questions.explanation: Section 1(3) specifies enforcement date of 1st July 1890.

questions.question_text: Under Section 3 of GWA 1890, the provisions of the Act are read subject to enactments relating to:
options: Court of Wards and jurisdiction of Chartered High Courts
questions.explanation: Section 3 saves jurisdiction of Court of Wards and Chartered High Courts.

questions.question_text: Under Section 4(2) of GWA 1890, 'guardian' means a person having the care of:
options: The person of a minor, or of his property, or of both his person and property
questions.explanation: Section 4(2) defines guardian covering person, property, or both.

questions.question_text: Under Section 4(3) of GWA 1890, 'ward' means:
options: A minor for whose person or property, or both, there is a guardian
questions.explanation: Section 4(3) defines ward as a minor with a guardian.

questions.question_text: Under Section 4(6) of GWA 1890, 'Collector' includes any officer appointed by State Government to be Collector for the purposes of the Act in respect of:
options: Revenue administration of a district or specified local area
questions.explanation: Section 4(6) defines Collector for revenue district purposes.

questions.question_text: Under Section 6 of GWA 1890, does anything in the Act take away any power to appoint a guardian of a minor's person or property under any personal law?
options: Yes, GWA repeals all personal laws
No, Section 6 saves power to appoint in other cases under personal law or Will
Yes, Court must appoint in all cases
questions.explanation: Section 6 saves pre-existing personal law powers and testamentary appointments.

questions.question_text: Under Section 10(2) of GWA 1890, an application by a person desirous of being guardian must be accompanied by a declaration of willingness to act signed by:
options: The proposed guardian and attested by at least two witnesses
questions.explanation: Section 10(2) requires proposed guardian's signed & 2-witness attested willingness declaration.

questions.question_text: Under Section 13 of GWA 1890, before making an order on a guardianship application, the Court shall:
options: Decide on affidavits without hearing evidence
Hear such evidence as may be adduced in support of or in opposition to the application
questions.explanation: Section 13 mandates hearing evidence before passing guardianship orders.

questions.question_text: Under Section 16 of GWA 1890, if a minor has property outside the local limits of the Court's jurisdiction:
options: The Court may appoint a guardian for property within jurisdiction and request another District Court to appoint for property outside
The Court cannot act at all
questions.explanation: Section 16 details handling property beyond local territorial limits.

questions.question_text: Under Section 19(c) of GWA 1890, the Court is NOT authorized to appoint a guardian of the person of a minor whose property is under the superintendence of:
options: A Court of Wards competent to appoint a guardian of the person of the minor
questions.explanation: Section 19(c) bars the Court from appointing a guardian of the person where the minor's property is under a Court of Wards competent to appoint such a guardian.

questions.question_text: Under Section 19(a) of GWA 1890, the Court is NOT authorized to appoint a guardian of the person of a minor who is a MARRIED FEMALE whose husband is:
options: Not, in the opinion of the Court, unfit to be guardian of her person
questions.explanation: Section 19(a) bars the Court from appointing a guardian of the person of a minor married female whose husband is not, in the opinion of the Court, unfit.

questions.question_text: Under Section 23 of GWA 1890, a Collector appointed as guardian of property is subject to the control of:
options: The State Government or such authority as State Government appoints
questions.explanation: Section 23 subjects Collector guardian to State Government administrative control.

questions.question_text: Under Section 25(2) of GWA 1890, for the purpose of enforcing an order for the return of a ward to custody, the Court may:
options: Exercise the powers of a Magistrate of the First Class under Section 100 of CrPC (search warrant for wrongfully confined person)
questions.explanation: Section 25(2) equips court with CrPC Magistrate search warrant powers to locate and retrieve ward.

questions.question_text: Under Section 32 of GWA 1890, the Court may from time to time by order vary or add to the powers of a court-appointed property guardian regarding:
options: Management and disposal of minor's property
questions.explanation: Section 32 empowers court to alter or extend property management powers.

questions.question_text: Under Section 34(e) of GWA 1890, a property guardian must pay into Court the balance due from him on his accounts at such times as:
questions.explanation: Section 34(e) requires the guardian, if so required, to pay into Court the balance due from him on his accounts at such time as the Court directs.

questions.question_text: Under Section 34A of GWA 1890 (inserted in 1929), the Court may award reasonable remuneration to:
options: An auditor appointed to audit a guardian's accounts
questions.explanation: Section 34A enables court to pay remuneration to account auditors.

questions.question_text: Under Section 36(1) of GWA 1890, where NO administration-bond was taken from a guardian under Section 34, a suit for an account against the guardian may be instituted by:
options: The ward on attaining majority, or with leave of Court during minority by any relative/friend
questions.explanation: Section 36(1) provides procedure for account suits when no bond was taken.

questions.question_text: Under Section 39(h) of GWA 1890, a guardian may be removed if he ceases to reside within:
options: The local limits of the jurisdiction of the Court
questions.explanation: Section 39(h) includes ceasing to reside within jurisdiction as a removal ground.

questions.question_text: Under Section 41(3) of GWA 1890, when a guardian's authority ceases, the Court may compel him or his representative to:
options: Deliver all property in his possession/control and all accounts to the person entitled thereto
Sign a bond of Rs. 1 Lakh
questions.explanation: Section 41(3) empowers court to compel delivery of property and accounts upon cessation.

questions.question_text: Under Section 42 of GWA 1890, when a guardian dies, is discharged, or is removed, the Court may:
options: Transfer minor to state care automatically
Appoint or declare another guardian in his place
questions.explanation: Section 42 provides for appointing a successor guardian.

questions.question_text: Under Section 49 of GWA 1890, the costs of any proceeding under the Act are in the discretion of:
questions.explanation: Section 49 places proceeding costs within judicial discretion.

questions.question_text: Under Section 51 of GWA 1890, a guardian already appointed by a Court before commencement of the Act shall be deemed to be:
options: A guardian appointed under this Act
questions.explanation: Section 51 contains savings provision for pre-1890 court-appointed guardians.

questions.question_text: In Githa Hariharan v. Reserve Bank of India (1999) 2 SCC 228, the Supreme Court interpreted Section 6(a) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 and Section 19(b) of GWA 1890 to hold that:
options: Mother can never be natural guardian while father lives

The word 'after' in 'father and after him, the mother' means 'in the absence of' (including physical absence, indifference, or incapacity), according equal guardianship status to mother under Articles 14 and 15
questions.explanation: Githa Hariharan (1999) established gender-equal interpretation of natural guardianship under Articles 14 & 15.
questions.statute_or_case: Githa Hariharan v. Reserve Bank of India (1999) 2 SCC 228

questions.question_text: Can a District Court grant permission under Section 29 to sell a minor's land merely because a buyer offers a high price if there is no necessity or advantage to the minor?
options: Yes, high price alone justifies sale
No, Section 31(1) strictly forbids granting permission unless there is necessity or evident advantage to the minor
questions.explanation: Section 31(1) mandates proof of necessity or evident advantage to minor; high price alone is insufficient.

questions.question_text: Under Section 7(3) of GWA 1890, where a guardian has already been appointed by will, the Court shall not appoint or declare another person to be guardian in his stead until:
options: The minor attains the age of 12 years
The powers of the guardian appointed by will have ceased under the provisions of the Act
questions.explanation: Section 7(3) bars appointing a substitute guardian until the powers of the existing testamentary (or court-appointed) guardian have ceased under the Act.

questions.question_text: Under Section 9(3) of GWA 1890, if an application for property guardianship is made to a court where property is situated, but the minor ordinarily resides elsewhere:
options: The Court may return the application to be presented to the Court where minor ordinarily resides
questions.explanation: Section 9(3) enables court to return application for filing at ordinary residence court.

questions.question_text: Under Section 25 of GWA 1890, does a de facto guardian have a statutory right to apply for custody of a minor under Section 25?
options: Yes, de facto guardian has equal rights
Yes, de facto guardian preferred over natural guardian
Section 25 specifies 'a guardian of the person' (lawful/court-appointed or natural guardian); de facto guardians lack Section 25 statutory custody rights
De facto guardian gets automatic custody
questions.explanation: Section 25 custody remedy is reserved for lawful/natural/court-appointed guardians.

questions.question_text: Under Section 29 of GWA 1890, if a court-appointed guardian mortgages minor's land for 2 years without court permission, what can the minor do on reaching 18?
options: File a suit under Section 30 to set aside the mortgage as VOIDABLE
questions.explanation: Section 30 gives minor right to set aside unauthorized transfer as voidable.

questions.question_text: Under Section 31(3)(b) of GWA 1890, when permission is granted to sell minor's property by public auction, how is notice of sale published?
options: In such manner as Court prescribes
questions.explanation: Section 31(3)(b) specifies court-directed publication of sale notice.

questions.question_text: Under Section 33(2) of GWA 1890, if a guardian acts upon the opinion, advice, or direction given by the Court under Section 33(1):
options: He shall be deemed to have discharged his duty as guardian in respect of the matter (unless guilty of fraud/concealment)
questions.explanation: Section 33(2) protects guardian acting on court's advisory opinion from personal liability.

questions.question_text: Under Section 39(a) of GWA 1890, a guardian may be removed for 'abuse of his trust'. What constitutes abuse of trust?
options: Misappropriating minor's property or using minor's funds for personal benefit
questions.explanation: Section 39(a) abuse of trust covers fiduciary self-dealing and misappropriation.

questions.question_text: Under Section 39(g) of GWA 1890, a guardian may be removed if he has an interest ADVERSE to the faithful performance of his duties. What is an adverse interest?
options: Clashing financial or property claims against the minor's estate
questions.explanation: Section 39(g) specifies adverse financial/property conflict of interest as a removal ground.

questions.question_text: Under Section 41(1)(a) of GWA 1890, the authority of a guardian of the PERSON ceases by:
questions.explanation: Section 41(1)(a) specifies termination of person guardianship by death/removal/discharge.

questions.question_text: Under Section 45(1)(a) of GWA 1890, if a person fails to produce a minor when ordered by Court under Section 12, the Court may impose a daily fine AND:
options: Sentence him to 10 years hard labor
Commit him to civil jail until he produces the minor
questions.explanation: Section 45(1) empowers court to commit contumacious person to civil jail.

questions.question_text: Under Section 46 of GWA 1890, a District Court may call upon a subordinate Court or a Collector to submit a report on any matter arising in GWA proceedings, and such report:
options: May be treated as evidence in the proceeding
questions.explanation: Section 46 authorizes receiving Collector/Subordinate Court reports as evidence.

questions.question_text: Under Section 47(e) of GWA 1890, is an order under Section 29 refusing permission to sell minor's property APPEALABLE to the High Court?
options: Appealable to the Supreme Court only
Yes, Section 47(e) includes an order under Section 28 or Section 29 refusing permission to a guardian to do an act referred to in the section
questions.explanation: Section 47(e) lists refusal of permission under Section 28 or Section 29 as an appealable order.

questions.question_text: Does the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 apply to Muslim minors as well as Hindu minors?
options: Yes, GWA 1890 is a secular statutory framework governing guardianship applications for minors of all religions in India
No, Muslim minors governed by Shariat Act exclusively
questions.explanation: GWA 1890 provides procedural and statutory machinery for guardianship applications across all communities.
questions.statute_or_case: Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 Preamble & Section 1

questions.question_text: When a court considers a custody application under Section 25 GWA between a Muslim father and mother, what prevails if Muslim personal law custody rules conflict with child's welfare?
options: Child's welfare prevails paramountly over personal law custody rules, as consistently held by the Supreme Court (e.g. Rosy Jacob v. Jacob A. Chakramakkal)
questions.explanation: Supreme Court has repeatedly affirmed that under GWA 1890, child's welfare is the supreme consideration overriding personal law technicalities.

questions.question_text: Under Section 9(1) of GWA 1890, if a child was residing in Delhi for 5 years and was forcefully removed to Mumbai 2 weeks before application, which Court has jurisdiction?
options: Delhi District Court, because Delhi is where the minor 'ordinarily resides' (temporary forced removal does not change ordinary residence)
questions.explanation: Ordinary residence means place of settled residence; temporary or fraudulent removal does not shift ordinary residence jurisdiction.

questions.question_text: Under Section 12(1) of GWA 1890, can the Court order the interim protection of minor's property before appointing a final guardian?
options: No, property orders only at final judgment
No, property goes to the State
No, a bank manages the property
Yes, Section 12(1) empowers the Court to make such order for the temporary custody and protection of the person or property of the minor as it thinks proper
questions.explanation: Section 12(1) authorises interlocutory orders for the temporary custody and protection of the minor's person or property.

questions.question_text: Under Section 17(2) of GWA 1890, if the minor's deceased father expressed a wish in his Will regarding guardian appointment, how does the Court treat it?
options: The Court shall have regard to the wishes of a deceased parent
Court is bound 100% even if guardian is unfit
questions.explanation: Section 17(2) mandates giving regard to deceased parent's wishes subject to welfare.

questions.question_text: Under Section 25(1) of GWA 1890, can a guardian file a custody application if the ward was removed from custody BEFORE the guardian was formally appointed by Court?
options: No, must be court-appointed before removal
Yes, if the applicant was a natural guardian entitled to custody when ward was removed
No, natural guardians cannot use Section 25
questions.explanation: Natural guardians entitled to custody can invoke Section 25 when ward is removed.

questions.question_text: Under Section 29 of GWA 1890, if a court-appointed guardian wants to sell minor's land to pay for minor's higher education abroad:
options: He can sell directly without permission
He must get permission from minor's school
He must apply for and obtain previous permission of the Court under Section 29 & 31
He must get permission from bank
questions.explanation: Sale of minor's land for education requires prior court permission under Sections 29 & 31.

questions.question_text: Under Section 31(3) of GWA 1890, can the Court attach conditions to its permission to sell minor's land (e.g. requiring sale proceeds to be paid into Court or invested on prescribed securities)?
options: No, the Court cannot attach conditions
Conditions are attached by the bank only
Conditions are attached by the buyer only
Yes, Section 31(3) lets the Court attach conditions, including that the proceeds be paid into Court or invested by the Court on prescribed securities
questions.explanation: Section 31(3)(d) allows the Court to direct that the whole or part of the sale proceeds be paid into Court or invested on prescribed securities.

questions.question_text: Under Section 39(c) of GWA 1890, a guardian may be removed for 'continuous failure to perform his duties'. What is continuous failure?
options: Persistent neglect of ward's health, education, support, or property management
questions.explanation: Section 39(c) targets systemic and persistent neglect of guardianship obligations.

questions.question_text: Under Section 41(1)(e) of GWA 1890, the authority of a guardian of the person ceases when the minor's father:
options: Was unfit, but ceases to be unfit in the opinion of the Court
questions.explanation: Section 41(1)(e) provides guardianship ceases if father ceases to be unfit.

questions.question_text: Under Section 43(2) of GWA 1890, where there are two or more guardians of a ward who cannot agree on a question affecting his welfare, what may be done?
options: The guardianship of all of them lapses
The ward is placed in State care
Any of the guardians may apply to the Court, which may make such order respecting the matter in difference as it thinks fit
questions.explanation: Section 43(2) allows any of several disagreeing guardians to apply to the Court, which resolves the matter in difference as it thinks fit.

questions.question_text: Under Section 47(a) of GWA 1890, is an order refusing to appoint or declare a guardian under Section 7 APPEALABLE to High Court?
options: Yes, Section 47(a) explicitly permits appeal against an order under Section 7 refusing to appoint/declare a guardian
questions.explanation: Section 47(a) explicitly lists refusal under Section 7 as an appealable order.

questions.question_text: What is the primary overarching object of The Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 as stated in its Preamble?
options: To consolidate and amend the law relating to guardian and ward
questions.explanation: The Preamble states GWA 1890 is 'An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to guardian and ward'.

questions.question_text: Under Section 11(i) of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, if the adoption is of a son, the adoptive father or mother must not have:
options: A Hindu son, son's son or son's son's son (by legitimate blood or adoption) living at the time of adoption
questions.explanation: Section 11(i) mandates that if adopting a son, the adopter must not have a living Hindu son, grandson, or great-grandson.

questions.question_text: Under Section 18 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, a Hindu wife is entitled to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime, and may live separately without forfeiting her claim if:
options: He is guilty of desertion or cruelty
He has another wife living or keeps a concubine
He has ceased to be a Hindu by conversion
questions.explanation: Section 18(2) specifies statutory grounds on which a Hindu wife may live separately and claim maintenance.

questions.question_text: According to Section 1(2) of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, the Act extends to:
questions.explanation: Section 1(2) states that the Act extends to the whole of India.

questions.question_text: Under Section 2(1) of HAMA 1956, the Act applies to which of the following persons?
options: Virashaivas, Lingayats, Brahmo, Prarthana or Arya Samajists
Buddhists, Jains, and Sikhs by religion
Abandoned children brought up as Hindu, Buddhist, Jain or Sikh
questions.explanation: Section 2(1) applies to Hindus in all forms, Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs, and abandoned children brought up in these religions (cl. bb).

questions.question_text: Under Section 2(2) of HAMA 1956, the Act does NOT apply to members of which category unless the Central Government by notification directs?
options: Scheduled Tribes within the meaning of Article 366(25) of the Constitution
questions.explanation: Section 2(2) expressly exempts Scheduled Tribes under Article 366(25) from HAMA unless notified.

questions.question_text: Under Section 3(b) of HAMA 1956, 'maintenance' in all cases includes provision for food, clothing, residence, education, and medical attendance, and in the case of an unmarried daughter, also includes:
options: Reasonable expenses of and incident to her marriage
questions.explanation: Section 3(b)(ii) defines maintenance for an unmarried daughter to include reasonable marriage expenses.

questions.question_text: Under Section 3(c) of HAMA 1956, a 'minor' means a person who has not completed the age of:
questions.explanation: Section 3(c) defines minor as a person who has not completed 18 years of age.

questions.question_text: Under Section 4 of HAMA 1956, the overriding effect of the Act implies that any text, rule, interpretation, custom or usage of Hindu law in force immediately before commencement shall:
options: Cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in the Act
Continue to override the Act in family matters
Apply only to joint family property
questions.explanation: Section 4 provides an explicit overriding clause over prior Hindu law texts, rules, and customs.

questions.question_text: Under Section 5(1) of HAMA 1956, an adoption made after the commencement of the Act in contravention of Chapter II is:
options: Voidable at option of adopted child
questions.explanation: Section 5(1) declares any adoption made in contravention of Chapter II provisions to be null and void.

questions.question_text: Under Section 5(2) of HAMA 1956, an adoption which is void shall:
options: Transfer birth family property to adoptive family
Disqualify the child from inheriting anywhere
Neither create any rights in adoptive family nor destroy rights in family of birth
Vested absolute title in adoptive father
questions.explanation: Section 5(2) clarifies that a void adoption neither creates adoptive rights nor severs birth family rights.

questions.question_text: Under Section 6 of HAMA 1956, how many requisites are specified for a valid adoption?
options: Five requisites (Panchayat consent, Court order, Will, Age, Blood test)
Four requisites (Capacity to adopt, capacity to give, capacity to be adopted, and compliance with other conditions)
questions.explanation: Section 6 lists four mandatory requisites for any valid Hindu adoption.

questions.question_text: Under Section 7 of HAMA 1956, a male Hindu who is of sound mind and not a minor may adopt a son or daughter, provided that if he has a wife living, he shall NOT adopt except with her consent UNLESS:
options: The wife has completely renounced the world, ceased to be a Hindu, or been declared of unsound mind by a court
She is living at her parent's house for more than 1 month
questions.explanation: Section 7 proviso sets out the three strict statutory exceptions where wife's consent is dispensed with.

questions.question_text: Under Section 7 Explanation of HAMA 1956, if a male Hindu has more than one wife living at the time of adoption:
options: Consent of senior wife only is sufficient
The consent of all the wives is necessary (unless any proviso exception applies)
Consent of junior wife only is sufficient
No consent of any wife is required
questions.explanation: Section 7 Explanation requires consent of ALL living wives unless exempted under the proviso.

questions.question_text: Under Section 8 of HAMA 1956 (as substituted by Act 30 of 2010), any female Hindu who is of sound mind and not a minor has capacity to take in adoption, provided if she has a husband living she shall not adopt EXCEPT:
options: Without anyone's consent in all cases
With consent of her husband (unless husband renounced world, ceased to be Hindu, or declared unsound mind)
questions.explanation: The 2010 amendment to Section 8 placed married women on equal footing, requiring husband's consent unless exempted.
questions.statute_or_case: Section 8, HAMA 1956 (as amended by Act 30 of 2010)

questions.question_text: Under Section 9(1) of HAMA 1956, who amongst the following have the capacity to give a child in adoption?
options: Only the father or mother or the guardian of a child
questions.explanation: Section 9(1) strictly restricts capacity to give in adoption to father, mother, or guardian.

questions.question_text: Under Section 9(2) of HAMA 1956 (as amended in 2010), the father or mother, if alive, shall have:
options: Equal right to give a son or daughter in adoption with consent of the other
Mother's exclusive right for daughters only
Right exercisable only after child turns 10
questions.explanation: Section 9(2) as amended in 2010 grants equal right to father and mother to give in adoption with mutual consent.

questions.question_text: Under Section 9(4) of HAMA 1956, when can a guardian give a child in adoption?
options: At guardian's sole discretion without court permission
Where parents are dead, renounced world, abandoned child, declared unsound mind, or parentage unknown, WITH previous permission of Court
Only if child is over 16 years
questions.explanation: Section 9(4) permits a guardian to give a child in adoption only with prior permission of the court.

questions.question_text: Under Section 9(5) of HAMA 1956, before granting permission to a guardian to give a child in adoption, the Court must be satisfied that:
options: The adoptive parents pay a fixed fee to the State
The adoption will be for the welfare of the child and no unauthorized payment/reward has been received or given
questions.explanation: Section 9(5) mandates that child welfare is paramount and prohibits commercialization of adoption.

questions.question_text: Under Section 9 Explanation (ii) of HAMA 1956, 'Court' for granting permission to give a child in adoption means:
options: City Civil Court or District Court within whose local limits the child to be adopted ordinarily resides
questions.explanation: Section 9 Explanation (ii) defines Court based on ordinary residence of the child to be adopted.

questions.question_text: Under Section 10 of HAMA 1956, which of the following is a prerequisite for a person to be capable of being taken in adoption?
options: He or she is a Hindu, has not already been adopted, has not been married, and has not completed 15 years (unless custom permits)
He or she must be a minor under 5 years
He or she must be male only
He or she must belong to same gotra
questions.explanation: Section 10 sets out the four conditions: Hindu, not already adopted, unmarried, and under 15 years (subject to custom).

questions.question_text: Under Section 10(iii) & (iv) of HAMA 1956, can a person who is married OR who has completed the age of 15 years be adopted?
options: Yes, if there is a custom or usage applicable to the parties which permits it
Yes, with High Court approval only
questions.explanation: Section 10 clauses (iii) and (iv) contain an express statutory exception allowing adoption of married or >15 year old persons if custom permits.

questions.question_text: Under Section 11(ii) of HAMA 1956, if the adoption is of a daughter, the adoptive father or mother must NOT have living at the time of adoption:
options: A Hindu daughter or son's daughter (whether by legitimate blood or adoption)
questions.explanation: Section 11(ii) prohibits adopting a daughter if the adopter already has a living Hindu daughter or granddaughter.

questions.question_text: Under Section 11(iii) of HAMA 1956, if the adoption is by a MALE and the person to be adopted is a FEMALE, what is the mandatory age difference required?
options: The adoptive father must be at least 21 years older than the person to be adopted
questions.explanation: Section 11(iii) mandates a minimum age gap of 21 years when a male adopts a female.

questions.question_text: Under Section 11(iv) of HAMA 1956, if the adoption is by a FEMALE and the person to be adopted is a MALE, the adoptive mother must be:
options: At least 21 years older than the person to be adopted
questions.explanation: Section 11(iv) mandates a minimum age gap of 21 years when a female adopts a male.

questions.question_text: Under Section 11(v) of HAMA 1956, can the same child be adopted simultaneously by two or more persons?
options: No, the same child may not be adopted simultaneously by two or more persons
questions.explanation: Section 11(v) strictly prohibits simultaneous adoption of the same child by multiple persons.

questions.question_text: Under Section 11(vi) of HAMA 1956, what physical act is essential for the validity of an adoption?
options: The child to be adopted must be actually given and taken in adoption by parents/guardian with intent to transfer family
questions.explanation: Section 11(vi) requires actual giving and taking of the child. The proviso clarifies Dattahomam is NOT essential.

questions.question_text: Is the performance of 'Dattahomam' (religious ceremony) mandatory for a valid Hindu adoption under HAMA 1956?
options: Yes, unless exempted by High Court
No, Section 11(vi) proviso expressly states Dattahomam shall NOT be essential
questions.explanation: Section 11(vi) proviso clearly lays down that Dattahomam performance is not essential for validity.

questions.question_text: Under Section 12 of HAMA 1956, an adopted child shall be deemed to be the child of his/her adoptive parent for all purposes with effect from:
options: The date of birth of the child
The date of death of adoptive father
The date of registration of deed
questions.explanation: Section 12 specifies that adoption takes legal effect from the exact date of adoption (no relation back doctrine).

questions.question_text: Under Section 12 proviso (a) of HAMA 1956, regarding marriage after adoption, an adopted child:
options: Can marry any relative of birth family
Cannot marry any person whom he/she could not have married if continuing in family of birth
Must marry within adoptive gotra only
Is exempt from sapinda marriage rules
questions.explanation: Section 12 proviso (a) preserves birth family marriage prohibitions (sapinda / prohibited degrees).

questions.question_text: Under Section 12 proviso (b) of HAMA 1956, any property which VESTED in the adopted child BEFORE the adoption:
options: Divests immediately and transfers to birth family brothers
Shall continue to vest in such person subject to attached obligations (e.g. maintenance)
questions.explanation: Section 12 proviso (b) protects property already vested in the adopted child prior to adoption.

questions.question_text: Under Section 12 proviso (c) of HAMA 1956, the adopted child shall NOT divest any person of any estate which:
options: Vested in him or her before the adoption
questions.explanation: Section 12 proviso (c) abolished the old doctrine of 'relation back' where adoption divested vested estates.

questions.question_text: Under Section 13 of HAMA 1956, does adoption deprive the adoptive father or mother of the power to dispose of their property by gift or Will?
options: No, adoption does not deprive adoptive parents of power to dispose of property inter vivos or by Will (subject to agreement)
Yes, adoptive child gets automatic veto power
Yes, all property becomes joint coparcenary property
Yes, parent can dispose only 25% of property
questions.explanation: Section 13 preserves adoptive parents' full ownership and power to dispose of their separate property.

questions.question_text: Under Section 14(1) of HAMA 1956, where a Hindu who has a wife living adopts a child, she shall be deemed to be the:
questions.explanation: Section 14(1) provides that wife living at time of adoption by husband is the adoptive mother.

questions.question_text: Under Section 14(2) of HAMA 1956, where an adoption is made with the consent of MORE THAN ONE wife living:
options: All wives are co-adoptive mothers equally
The youngest wife is adoptive mother
The seniormost in marriage shall be deemed adoptive mother, and others to be step-mothers
Court decides who is adoptive mother
questions.explanation: Section 14(2) designates the seniormost wife in marriage as adoptive mother.

questions.question_text: Under Section 14(3) of HAMA 1956, where a widower or a bachelor adopts a child, any wife whom he subsequently marries shall be deemed to be:
options: The step-mother of the adopted child
questions.explanation: Section 14(3) enacts that a wife subsequently married by a widower/bachelor adopter is a step-mother.

questions.question_text: Under Section 14(4) of HAMA 1956, where a widow or an unmarried woman adopts a child, any husband whom she marries subsequently shall be deemed to be:
options: The step-father of the adopted child
questions.explanation: Section 14(4) enacts that a husband subsequently married by a widow/unmarried woman adopter is a step-father.

questions.question_text: Under Section 15 of HAMA 1956, can a validly made adoption be cancelled by the adoptive father/mother OR renounced by the adopted child?
options: Yes, within 1 year by mutual consent
No, a valid adoption cannot be cancelled by anyone, nor can the adopted child renounce status and return to birth family
Yes, if adopted child turns out to be disrespectful
Yes, by civil court decree on payment of fine
questions.explanation: Section 15 makes a valid adoption irrevocable by adoptive parents or child.

questions.question_text: Under Section 16 of HAMA 1956, when a registered document recording adoption signed by giving and taking parties is produced before a court:
options: The document is void unless approved by Collector
The court shall presume that the adoption compliance was made unless and until it is disproved
questions.explanation: Section 16 creates a statutory mandatory presumption ('shall presume') in favour of registered adoption deeds.

questions.question_text: Under Section 17 of HAMA 1956, receiving or giving any payment or reward in consideration of adoption is prohibited. Any person contravening this provision is punishable with:
options: Imprisonment up to six months, or with fine, or both
questions.explanation: Section 17(2) prescribes punishment up to 6 months imprisonment, or fine, or both.

questions.question_text: Under Section 17(3) of HAMA 1956, no prosecution for taking or giving reward for adoption shall be instituted without:
options: Previous sanction of the State Government or an authorized officer
questions.explanation: Section 17(3) requires prior State Government sanction before instituting prosecution.

questions.question_text: Under Section 18(1) of HAMA 1956, a Hindu wife is entitled to be maintained by her husband:
options: During her lifetime (whether married before or after commencement of the Act)
Only if she has borne sons
Only if husband has ancestral property
questions.explanation: Section 18(1) creates a personal statutory obligation on husband to maintain wife for her lifetime.

questions.question_text: Under Section 18(3) of HAMA 1956, a Hindu wife forfeits her entitlement to separate residence and maintenance if she:
options: Is unchaste OR ceases to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion
questions.explanation: Section 18(3) lists two statutory disqualifications: unchastity or conversion.

questions.question_text: Under Section 19(1) of HAMA 1956, a Hindu widowed daughter-in-law is entitled to be maintained after her husband's death by her father-in-law to the extent that she cannot maintain herself out of her earnings/property or from:
options: Estate of her husband, father, mother, or her son/daughter
questions.explanation: Section 19(1) proviso outlines sources of maintenance that precede father-in-law's liability.

questions.question_text: Under Section 19(2) of HAMA 1956, father-in-law's obligation to maintain widowed daughter-in-law is enforceable ONLY if he has means from coparcenary property in his possession AND the obligation CEASES on her:
questions.explanation: Section 19(2) provides that the maintenance obligation of father-in-law ceases upon her remarriage.

questions.question_text: Under Section 20(1) of HAMA 1956, a Hindu is bound during lifetime to maintain his or her:
options: Legitimate or illegitimate children and aged or infirm parents
questions.explanation: Section 20(1) imposes statutory duty to maintain minor children (legitimate/illegitimate) and aged/infirm parents.

questions.question_text: Under Section 20(2) of HAMA 1956, a legitimate or illegitimate child may claim maintenance from father or mother so long as the child is:
questions.explanation: Section 20(2) limits child's general maintenance right to minority (under 18 years).

questions.question_text: Under Section 20(3) of HAMA 1956, obligation to maintain an UNMARRIED DAUGHTER extends so long as she is unable to maintain herself. Does this right extend beyond minority?
options: No, it ends strictly at 18 years
Only if she is physically disabled
Yes, an unmarried daughter can claim maintenance even after attaining majority if unable to maintain herself
questions.explanation: Section 20(3) extends maintenance obligation for unmarried daughter beyond majority until marriage if unable to maintain herself.

questions.question_text: Under Section 20 Explanation of HAMA 1956, 'parent' for the purpose of maintenance includes:
questions.explanation: Section 20 Explanation explicitly includes a childless step-mother within 'parent'.

questions.question_text: How many categories of relatives of a deceased Hindu are defined as 'dependants' under Section 21 of HAMA 1956?
questions.explanation: Section 21 defines 9 specific categories of dependants of a deceased Hindu.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT listed as a 'dependant' under Section 21 of HAMA 1956?
options: Widow (so long as she does not remarried)
Major married son capable of earning
questions.explanation: Section 21 includes minor sons, but NOT major married earning sons.

questions.question_text: Under Section 22(1) of HAMA 1956, the heirs of a deceased Hindu are bound to maintain dependants of the deceased out of:
options: The estate inherited by them from the deceased
questions.explanation: Section 22(1) ties maintenance liability of heirs directly to the estate inherited from deceased.

questions.question_text: Under Section 22(3) of HAMA 1956, the liability of each heir who takes the estate to maintain dependants shall be:
options: In proportion to the value of the share or part of the estate taken by him or her
Equal among all heirs regardless of share
Borne entirely by the eldest male heir
Borne by executor of Will only
questions.explanation: Section 22(3) mandates proportional liability based on share value taken by each heir.

questions.question_text: Under Section 23(2) of HAMA 1956, in determining the quantum of maintenance for a wife, children, or aged parents, the Court shall have regard to:
options: Position/status of parties, reasonable wants, separate living justification, claimant's property/income, and number of entitled persons
Only income tax return of husband
questions.explanation: Section 23(2) sets out 5 statutory factors court must consider when fixing maintenance amount.

questions.question_text: Under Section 24 of HAMA 1956, no person shall be entitled to claim maintenance under Chapter III if he or she has:
options: Ceased to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion
questions.explanation: Section 24 disentitles any claimant who ceases to be a Hindu by conversion.

questions.question_text: Under Section 25 of HAMA 1956, the amount of maintenance (whether fixed by court decree or agreement) may be altered subsequently if:
options: There is a material change in the circumstances justifying such alteration
questions.explanation: Section 25 permits modification of maintenance decree/agreement upon material change of circumstances.

questions.question_text: Under Section 26 of HAMA 1956, debts of every description contracted or payable by the deceased shall have:
options: Priority over claims of his dependants for maintenance (subject to Section 27 charge)
questions.explanation: Section 26 gives priority to deceased's debts over maintenance claims unless a charge is created under s. 27.

questions.question_text: Under Section 27 of HAMA 1956, a dependant's claim for maintenance is NOT a charge on the estate of the deceased UNLESS:
options: A charge has been created by Will, court decree, agreement, or otherwise
questions.explanation: Section 27 specifies that maintenance is not an automatic charge unless specifically created.

questions.question_text: Under Section 28 of HAMA 1956, right to receive maintenance out of transferred estate can be enforced against a transferee IF the transferee has notice of right OR transfer is gratuitous, BUT NOT against:
options: A transferee for consideration and without notice of the right (bona fide purchaser for value without notice)
questions.explanation: Section 28 protects bona fide purchasers for consideration without notice from maintenance claims.

questions.question_text: Under Section 30 of HAMA 1956 (Savings), nothing in the Act affects any adoption made BEFORE the commencement of the Act. Such pre-1956 adoptions are determined as if:
options: The Act had not been passed
questions.explanation: Section 30 saves pre-1956 adoptions, leaving their validity to prior Hindu law.

questions.question_text: In Abhilasha v. Parkash (2020 SCC OnLine SC 736), the Supreme Court held that an unmarried Hindu daughter can claim maintenance from her father beyond majority under:
options: Section 20(3) of HAMA 1956, which can be enforced by Family Court
Section 125 CrPC directly without reference to HAMA
questions.explanation: Abhilasha v. Parkash (2020) harmonized CrPC 125 and HAMA S. 20(3) allowing unmarried major daughter maintenance under HAMA.
questions.statute_or_case: Abhilasha v. Parkash, 2020 SCC OnLine SC 736

questions.question_text: In Sawan Ram v. Kalawanti (1967) 3 SCR 687, the Supreme Court held that when a Hindu widow adopts a child under HAMA 1956, the adopted child becomes the child of:
options: The widow only, having no relation to deceased husband
The widow and also of her deceased husband
questions.explanation: Sawan Ram (1967) established that child adopted by a widow is tied to her deceased husband's family.

questions.question_text: In Padmja Sharma v. Ratan Lal Sharma (2000) 4 SCC 266, the Supreme Court held that under Section 20 of HAMA 1956, the obligation to maintain children when BOTH parents are employed is:
options: Shared by both father and mother in proportion to their respective incomes
questions.explanation: Padmja Sharma held that both earning parents are duty bound to contribute proportionately to child maintenance.
questions.statute_or_case: Padmja Sharma v. Ratan Lal Sharma, (2000) 4 SCC 266

questions.question_text: Under Section 16 of HAMA 1956 as amended in Uttar Pradesh (U.P. Act 57 of 1976), in respect of adoptions made on or after 01.01.1977, UP Courts shall NOT accept any evidence of giving and taking EXCEPT:
options: A registered document recording adoption signed by giving and taking parties
questions.explanation: UP State Amendment to Section 16 made registered adoption deed mandatory proof of adoption.

questions.question_text: Under Section 18(2)(d) of HAMA 1956, a Hindu wife may live separately and claim maintenance if her husband has:
options: Adopted a child without her knowledge
questions.explanation: Section 18(2)(d) gives a statutory ground for separate residence if husband has another living wife.

questions.question_text: Under Section 18(2)(e) of HAMA 1956, a Hindu wife is entitled to live separately without forfeiting maintenance if her husband keeps a concubine:
options: In the same house in which his wife is living OR habitually resides with a concubine elsewhere
questions.explanation: Section 18(2)(e) grants ground for separate maintenance if husband keeps/resides with concubine.

questions.question_text: Under Section 18(2)(f) of HAMA 1956, a Hindu wife can claim separate residence and maintenance if her husband:
options: Has ceased to be a Hindu by conversion to another religion
questions.explanation: Section 18(2)(f) provides conversion of husband to another religion as a valid ground.

questions.question_text: Under Section 18(2)(g) of HAMA 1956, separate residence and maintenance can be granted if:
options: Wife prefers living in metro city
There is any other cause justifying her living separately (residuary clause)
questions.explanation: Section 18(2)(g) is a residuary clause giving wide judicial discretion for just causes.

questions.question_text: Can a step-mother claim maintenance under Section 20 of HAMA 1956?
options: Yes, if she is a childless step-mother unable to maintain herself
Only if she has adopted the step-son
questions.explanation: Section 20 Explanation includes childless step-mother within 'parent' entitled to maintenance.

questions.question_text: Under Section 21(vi) of HAMA 1956, a widowed daughter is a dependant of her deceased father provided and to the extent she is unable to obtain maintenance from:
options: Estate of her husband, her children/their estate, or her father-in-law/his father
questions.explanation: Section 21(vi) lists primary sources (husband, children, father-in-law) before father's estate liability arises.

questions.question_text: Under Section 21(viii) & (ix) of HAMA 1956, minor illegitimate sons and unmarried illegitimate daughters of a deceased Hindu are defined as:
options: Dependants entitled to maintenance out of deceased's estate
questions.explanation: Section 21(viii) & (ix) explicitly include minor illegitimate sons and unmarried illegitimate daughters as dependants.

questions.question_text: Under Section 22(4) of HAMA 1956, a person who is himself/herself a dependant shall NOT be liable to contribute to maintenance of others if:
options: The share obtained is or would become less than what would be awarded to him/her as maintenance
questions.explanation: Section 22(4) protects low-share dependants from being forced to contribute to other dependants.

questions.question_text: Under Section 23(3) of HAMA 1956, in determining maintenance for a DEPENDANT out of deceased's estate, court considers net value of estate after providing for:
options: Payment of debts of the deceased
questions.explanation: Section 23(3)(a) requires deducting deceased's debts to arrive at net estate value for dependant maintenance.

questions.question_text: If a Hindu male has a living biological daughter, can he validly adopt another daughter under HAMA 1956?
options: No, Section 11(ii) strictly prohibits adopting a daughter if a daughter or son's daughter is living
questions.explanation: Section 11(ii) creates an absolute bar against adopting a second daughter if one is living.

questions.question_text: If a Hindu male has a living biological son, can he validly adopt another son under HAMA 1956?
options: Yes, if biological son is abroad
No, Section 11(i) prohibits adopting a son if a Hindu son, son's son, or son's son's son is living
questions.explanation: Section 11(i) creates an absolute bar against adopting a second son if male issue up to 3 generations is living.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old unmarried Hindu female wishes to adopt a 5-year-old boy. Is this adoption valid under HAMA 1956?
options: No, female can adopt female child only
No, age gap must be 30 years
Yes, she has capacity under Section 8, and the age gap is 25 years (exceeding required 21 years under Section 11(iv))
questions.explanation: Under Section 8 & Section 11(iv), an unmarried female can adopt a male child if she is at least 21 years older (30 - 5 = 25 years).

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old bachelor Hindu male wishes to adopt a 10-year-old girl child. Is this adoption valid under HAMA 1956?
options: Yes, he has capacity under Section 7, and age gap is 25 years (exceeding required 21 years under Section 11(iii))
No, age gap must be 30 years
No, only married couples can adopt
questions.explanation: Under Section 7 & Section 11(iii), a bachelor male can adopt a female child provided he is at least 21 years older (35 - 10 = 25 years).

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old male Hindu adopts a 10-year-old girl child. Is this adoption valid under HAMA 1956?
options: No, because the age difference is only 15 years, violating the mandatory 21-year age gap required under Section 11(iii)
questions.explanation: Section 11(iii) requires male adopter to be at least 21 years older than female adopted child. 25 - 10 = 15 years, which is illegal and void.

questions.question_text: Does an adopted child under HAMA 1956 lose his right to inherit property from his biological parents which VESTED in him BEFORE adoption?
options: Yes, all birth property is forfeited
Yes, divests and goes to biological brothers
No, under Section 12 proviso (b), property vested before adoption continues to vest in him
questions.explanation: Section 12 proviso (b) preserves pre-vested property in the adopted child.

questions.question_text: Under HAMA 1956, can adoptive parents alter the statutory right of adoption by an agreement specifying that adopted child will not get ancestral property?
options: Yes, agreement can completely cancel adoption
No agreement is valid under HAMA
Section 13 permits agreements regarding disposition of adoptive parents' SEPARATE property, but cannot alter statutory coparcenary rights
questions.explanation: Section 13 allows agreements regarding adoptive parents' separate property disposition power.

questions.question_text: Under Section 18(2)(b) of HAMA 1956, cruelty as a ground for separate residence means treatment causing:
options: Reasonable apprehension in wife's mind that it will be harmful or injurious to live with her husband
questions.explanation: Section 18(2)(b) defines cruelty as treatment creating reasonable apprehension of injury or harm.

questions.question_text: Under Section 18(2)(a) of HAMA 1956, 'desertion' is defined as abandoning the wife:
options: Without reasonable cause and without her consent or against her wish, or wilfully neglecting her
questions.explanation: Section 18(2)(a) gives statutory definition of desertion for separate maintenance.

questions.question_text: If a Hindu husband converts to Islam, does his Hindu wife forfeit her right to maintenance under HAMA 1956?
options: Yes, marriage automatically dissolves without maintenance
No, husband's conversion is a specific ground for wife to live separately and claim maintenance under Section 18(2)(f)
She gets maintenance for 3 months only
questions.explanation: Husband's conversion gives wife a right to separate maintenance under S. 18(2)(f). Only WIFE'S conversion forfeits maintenance under S. 18(3).

questions.question_text: If a Hindu wife entitled to maintenance converts to Christianity, what is the legal effect under Section 18(3) of HAMA 1956?
options: She forfeits her claim to separate residence and maintenance under Section 18(3)
questions.explanation: Section 18(3) explicitly forfeits wife's maintenance if she ceases to be a Hindu by conversion.

questions.question_text: Under Section 21(vii) of HAMA 1956, a widow of a pre-deceased son is a dependant of deceased Hindu so long as she:
options: Does NOT remarry and is unable to obtain maintenance from her husband's estate, son/daughter, or father-in-law's estate
questions.explanation: Section 21(vii) defines son's widow as dependant conditional on non-remarriage and inability to get maintenance elsewhere.

questions.question_text: Under Section 21(iii) of HAMA 1956, a widow of the deceased is a dependant so long as she:
options: Does not leave the matrimonial house
questions.explanation: Section 21(iii) specifies that deceased's widow is a dependant 'so long as she does not re-marry'.

questions.question_text: Under Section 23(1) of HAMA 1956, determining whether any and what maintenance shall be awarded is:
options: Fixed strictly at 25% of husband's salary in all cases
In the discretion of the Court having regard to statutory factors
questions.explanation: Section 23(1) vests judicial discretion in Court to determine maintenance amount based on statutory guidelines.

questions.question_text: Under Section 9(3) of HAMA 1956 (prior to 2010 amendment, now omitted), mother could give child in adoption if father was dead/unsound/renounced. Post-2010 amendment, mother's right to give in adoption is:
options: Equal to father during lifetime with mutual consent
questions.explanation: Act 30 of 2010 substituted Section 9(2) giving father and mother equal rights during lifetime.

questions.question_text: Under Section 2(1)(bb) of HAMA 1956 (inserted by Act 45 of 1962), an abandoned child or child of unknown parentage is covered by HAMA if:
options: Brought up as a Hindu, Buddhist, Jaina or Sikh
questions.explanation: Section 2(1)(bb) covers abandoned children brought up in Hindu/Buddhist/Jain/Sikh faith.

questions.question_text: Under Section 10(ii) of HAMA 1956, can a child who has ALREADY been validly adopted be adopted a SECOND time by another family?
options: Yes, with consent of first adoptive parents
No, Section 10(ii) requires that the person has NOT already been adopted
Yes, if first adoptive father dies
questions.explanation: Section 10(ii) prohibits second adoption of an already adopted child.

questions.question_text: Under Section 12 proviso (c) of HAMA 1956, if A inherits property as sole surviving coparcener in 1960, and widow W adopts child X in 1965, does X divest A of his vested property?
options: Yes, X divests A of 50% share
Yes, X divests A of entire estate
No, Section 12 proviso (c) explicitly enacts that adopted child shall NOT divest any person of an estate vested before adoption
questions.explanation: Section 12 proviso (c) prevents divesting of property vested prior to adoption date.
